original_test_intent: Observe the approved SUT for12 idle hours and collect system/process memory and BMC event trends sufficient to identify sustained unexplained growth or unexpected error/garbage evidence.
original_method: Establish a timestamped baseline, collect periodic complete meminfo/free/swap/process or cgroup samples throughout12h, preserve workload/process lifecycle context and full SEL/log snapshots, then calculate trends without altering the DUT.
manual_activity: User defines idle state, scope and leak/garbage thresholds; agent can run the complete read-only12-hour collector after authorization.
required_inputs: Approved Linux/BMC host identity and secure access
Definition of idle state and permitted background activity
Sampling interval, process/cgroup scope and memory-growth threshold
procps/procfs and ipmitool/BMC privilege plus synchronized clocks
Protected evidence capacity, gap/invalid-run and verdict policy
safety_requirements: Verify exact host and idle-state eligibility
Use managed authentication/host verification and least privilege
Protect process command lines and BMC identifiers; preserve logs without clearing
Stop collector on wrong host, permission/storage/time-sync failure, monitoring gap or instability
No process restart, cache drop, SEL/log clear, reboot or automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Collect timestamped complete memory/process/cgroup/swap and SEL/log snapshots for12h
Report gaps and calculate trends with workload/lifecycle/cache context
Do not create load, infer leak from one metric, clear evidence, restart processes or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Define idle/sampling/threshold/garbage-data semantics and evidence policy
Resolve legitimate allocator/cache/process behavior versus suspected leak

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Insufficient and unsafe: a60-second tail-truncated pidstat plus one free sample cannot cover12h and omits complete SEL.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run a protected timestamped12-hour collector for full meminfo/free/swap/process or cgroup data and complete `ipmitool sel elist` snapshots with status/checksums.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Idle12h, free, IPMI SEL, leak/garbage assessment and30/750 fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use consistent periodic system and per-process/cgroup sampling plus start/end/full SEL snapshots and an explicit gap ledger.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds longitudinal evidence, attribution context, secure collection and invalid-run handling without changing state.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A one-minute sample cannot establish the source's12-hour behavior and is rejected.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Free memory is affected by cache/reclaim, RSS can include shared pages, PSS availability varies, and an idle-only run may miss workload-dependent leaks.

project_override_considerations: Project must define a measurable slope/delta and what `garbage data` means (for example unexpected SEL/ECC/log entries); the review does not declare normal allocator variation a leak.
expected_evidence: Declared idle state, active jobs/services and process lifecycle changes
Timestamped complete meminfo/free/swap/process RSS/PSS/cgroup samples for12h
Full start/intermediate/end IPMI SEL plus dmesg/syslog
Collector status, gaps, storage/checksums and trend calculations
Threshold comparison, caveats and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The12-hour idle observation and no-leak/no-garbage criterion are coherent, though numeric thresholds and garbage-data interpretation are project readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Host access, tools, scope, thresholds and storage can be supplied; the read-only collection is automatable.

review_improvement: Restores the source's full12-hour duration and SEL coverage and replaces single-point inference with attributable time-series evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A leak is a persistent retained-memory trend under comparable conditions, not simply a lower `free` value: Linux uses unused RAM for cache and allocators may retain arenas. Per-process/cgroup lifecycle plus meminfo and swap context is needed to distinguish retention from reclaimable cache, while SEL/ECC records address the separate source phrase `garbage data` as error evidence rather than memory contents.
